entries.title: Fatal hardware error (reported after restart)
entries.what: The system crashed because of a hardware error; this record was written after the restart.
fix: Remove overclock/XMP/undervolt
Check temperatures
Test RAM
Update BIOS

entries.title: Corrected PCI Express error
entries.what: A PCIe device or link had an error that was corrected. Frequent ones point to a flaky link.
causes: PCIe power saving (ASPM) on some boards/GPUs/NVMe
fix: Update BIOS and chipset drivers
Reseat the device named in the message
Try disabling PCIe Link State Power Management

entries.title: Fatal hardware error (machine check)
entries.what: The CPU reported a fatal machine check error. The system crashed.
fix: Reset BIOS to defaults (disable overclock/XMP)
Check CPU temperature and cooling
Update BIOS
Test RAM

entries.title: Corrected hardware error (CPU)
entries.what: The CPU detected and corrected an internal error (cache, bus). Occasional is tolerable; frequent means instability.
fix: Remove overclock, check temperatures, update BIOS

entries.title: Corrected memory error
entries.what: A RAM error was detected and corrected (ECC). Repeated errors indicate a failing memory module.
fix: Identify the module from the message; test or replace it

entries.title: Graphics driver stopped responding and recovered
entries.summary: Graphics driver {0} stopped responding and recovered
entries.what: The graphics driver hung; Windows reset it (TDR). The screen may have gone black for a moment.
fix: Clean-install the latest GPU driver (or a previous stable one)
Check GPU temperature; remove overclock
Check PSU and GPU power cables

entries.title: NVIDIA driver error
entries.what: The NVIDIA graphics driver reported an error or timeout (the GPU may have reset).
fix: Clean-install the NVIDIA driver (DDU, then latest stable)
Remove overclock; check temperatures and power cables

entries.title: Driver failed to load for a device
entries.summary: Driver {1} failed to load for a device
entries.what: A driver could not be loaded for a device at boot. Very often a virtual/user-mode driver (e.g. WUDFRd) that loads fine later - usually harmless.
causes: Device enumerated before its driver was ready
fix: Harmless if all devices work; otherwise check Device Manager for a yellow warning

entries.title: Application blocked device removal
entries.what: A program kept a device busy when it was being removed or ejected.

entries.title: Device configured
entries.what: A device was configured with a driver. Normal at boot and when plugging in devices.

entries.title: Device had a problem starting
entries.what: A device could not start. The message names the device and problem code.
fix: Check Device Manager; reinstall or update the driver

entries.title: Low virtual memory
entries.what: Windows was running out of memory. The message lists the programs using the most memory.
causes: A program with a memory leak
Page file disabled or too small
Not enough RAM for the workload
fix: Find the top consumer in the message and update/restart it
Set the page file to System managed
Add RAM if it happens under normal load

entries.title: Secure Boot certificate update failed
entries.what: Windows could not update the Secure Boot database (DB/DBX) on this device.
causes: Firmware does not accept the update
fix: Update BIOS/UEFI firmware
Check Secure Boot status in msinfo32

entries.title: Secure Boot certificates need updating
entries.what: The device's Secure Boot certificates have been flagged for update but not yet applied.
fix: Install the latest Windows updates and BIOS/UEFI firmware
